reason: Conversation 1 correctly identifies E:09 as a heating-circuit fault and names the heater/circulation-pump assembly as the leading suspect while flagging that the NTC sensor and wiring must be ruled out before parts are fitted, and it gives practical booking advice (model, code, both programmes cold, ask for a fixed diagnostic fee). Its weaknesses are over-caution in declining the isolated resistance test the ground truth deems acceptable and failing to give any repair-vs-replace cost steer despite being asked twice. Conversation 2 is safe and recommends an engineer, but mischaracterises the fix as 'the heating element itself, which is a standard replacement part' - on this model the heater is integral to the heat pump, so this understates the repair and matches a listed unsupported claim - and it ends after one turn with no diagnostic path or economics discussion.
